title: Home Office and Desk Organization for Brains With 47 Open Tabs
description: Desk organization for ADHD brains: a clear-desk system, a daily 3-thing board and 8 Amazon finds for cables, chargers and paper.
intro:
If your desk currently holds three mugs, a stack of mail, two chargers (neither for your phone), a hair clip and a sticky note that says "IMPORTANT" with nothing else on it... hi. Same.

Desks attract clutter because they're flat, central and we're usually thinking about something else while we're at them. Every object that lands there becomes one more thing tugging at our attention.

A clear-ish desk makes it easier to focus on the one thing in front of you. Here's how to set one up that stays that way (mostly).

sections.heading: The goal: only today's work on the desk
sections.body:
A focused desk holds three kinds of things:

1. What you're working on right now.
2. Tools you use every single day (pen, notebook, charger).
3. One small thing that makes you happy (a plant, a photo, a candle).

Everything else lives in drawers, on the wall or somewhere else entirely.

sections.heading: Step 1: The 15-minute desk clear
sections.body:
Set a timer. Grab a box and a trash bag.

- Trash goes in the bag.
- Mugs and dishes go to the kitchen (after the timer).
- Papers go into one pile, face down, to sort later.
- Anything that doesn't belong at the desk goes in the box.

When the timer ends, you'll have a clear surface. The paper pile gets its own session another day.

sections.heading: Step 2: Give cables a home
sections.body:
Cables are the invisible clutter that makes a desk feel messy even when it's clean. Try:

- A charging station for phones, earbuds and watches.
- A cable management box to hide the power strip.
- Adhesive cable clips on the desk edge so chargers don't fall behind.

This one step can make a desk look twice as tidy.

sections.heading: Step 3: Go vertical
sections.body:
A pegboard or wall shelf above the desk holds supplies you want to see without cluttering the surface. A monitor stand with a drawer tucks away the small stuff and lifts your screen to a better height.

For our brains, supplies on the wall are better than supplies in a drawer. We see them, so we use them, and we put them back.

sections.heading: Step 4: The 3-thing board
sections.body:
Put a small whiteboard next to your screen and write today's three most important tasks on it. Not ten. Three.

When you finish one, cross it off with gusto. When your brain drifts, the board pulls it back. It's a visible anchor in a world of open tabs.

sections.heading: Step 5: A paper inbox, not a paper pile
sections.body: Paper will always show up on the desk. Give it one tray labeled INBOX. Everything new goes there, instead of scattered across the surface. Once a week, empty the inbox using the toss-act-keep system.

sections.heading: The end-of-day shutdown (3 minutes)
sections.body:
Before you step away:

1. Cups to the kitchen.
2. Papers into the inbox.
3. Write tomorrow's three things on the board.
4. Push in the chair.

This tiny ritual also tells your brain the workday is over, which is a nice bonus when your office is also your dining room.

finds.name: Multi-device charging station
finds.why: Every device charges in one place, so you always know where your phone is.

finds.name: Cable management box
finds.search: cable management box for power strip
finds.why: The power strip goes in a box and the tangle disappears. Five-minute makeover.

finds.name: Adhesive cable clips
finds.why: Clips hold cables at the desk edge so they never slide back behind it.

finds.name: Small desktop whiteboard with stand
finds.why: A tiny board beside your screen keeps today's priorities in view, not in a lost app.

finds.name: Monitor stand with storage drawer
finds.search: monitor stand riser with storage drawer
finds.why: The riser frees up space and a drawer tucks away the clutter that was on the desk.

finds.name: Desk pegboard organizer
finds.why: See every tool at once. If you can see it, you'll put it back.

finds.name: Desk drawer organizer trays
finds.why: Trays give pens, clips and chargers their own spots so you find them in one look.

finds.name: Stackable letter trays
finds.why: One tray is your inbox. Add a second for action items and a third for filing. That's your desk paper system.

outro:
Clear the desk once, give cables a home and write three things on a board. Your future focus will thank you.

The *Tidy Brain Printable Pack* includes a daily "3 things" planner page and an end-of-day shutdown checklist if paper works better for you than a whiteboard.
